messages:
maria (support): FYI incoming escalation from AcroPay — streaming responses cut off mid-stream, client reconnects immediately and they see partial JSON objects. customer reports spikes when they use mobile clients over flaky LTE. request_id=rp_0a9c2b
ryan (oncall): Can you paste the request_id and an example client log? also which model/route and any recent deploys?
maria (support): request_id=rp_0a9c2b, route=/v1/streams/complete, model=gpt-xl-legacy, no deploys in last 24h. client log shows repeated "fetch stream ended unexpectedly" then a reconnect, HTTP 200 on reconnect. Server trace snippets: 
```
runtime: write short (sent=512/4096) -> errno=11, queued_bytes=4.8MB
runtime: stream soft-abort reason=socket_buffer_exceeded threshold=4MB
```
maya (eng-runtime): Hmm soft-abort indicates we hit our per-socket queued byte threshold and we closed to avoid mem blow. errno=11 is non-blocking EAGAIN on send(). is this client reading slowly?
amar (billing): Customer says they noticed a billing jump because reconnects counted as new sessions. we should confirm retry behavior.
maria (support): customer provided a minimal repro: Node fetch + slow consumer that reads one chunk every 2s. they forwarded a test script. says mobile SDK uses smaller recv windows and background throttling.
ryan (oncall): Steps to reproduce locally? can you attach the script here or a gist link?
maria (support): pasted gist: https://gist.example.com/acro/sse-slow-reader.js
--- gist content (summarized) ---
const res = await fetch(streamUrl)
const reader = res.body.getReader()
while(true){ const {done, value} = await reader.read(); await sleep(2000); /* slow processing */ if(done) break; console.log(value.length) }
--- end ---
maya (eng-runtime): Repro looks good. Local run produced same runtime logs: short writes then queued_bytes growing until we hit soft-abort. We normally allow some headroom but mobile connections with small TCP recv windows + paused JS event loop can starve reader.
ryan (oncall): Any immediate mitigations? Can we change soft-abort threshold or make server pause writing earlier?
maya (eng-runtime): Mitigations: 1) lower max in-memory queued_bytes for streaming routes (safer short term), 2) stream chunk smaller (reduce per-write size), 3) expose a perp-client header that opts into lower throughput, 4) recommend client-side keepalive/read loop to avoid OS-level stalls. We can also add server-side backpressure hints (503 Retry-After) but that affects UX.
amar (billing): If we lower threshold we might reduce billing inflation by preventing reconnect loops — but need to warn AcroPay.
ryan (oncall): For this customer can we: (A) reproduce with their payload/headers, (B) flip a per-customer lower buffered_bytes flag, (C) ask client to try enabling streaming ack or smaller chunking?
maria (support): I asked customer for their SDK version and platform. they confirmed SDK=js-mobile-1.2.1 on Android 11. said they cannot change read pacing easily.
maya (eng-runtime): Action items from runtime side: I'll add a temporary per-tenant soft-abort reduction to 1MB for their tenant to force earlier backpressure (maya -> will push feature flag for acropay:test). Also add better logging to include client recv window estimate + socket sndbuf at time of abort.
ryan (oncall): I'll coordinate a short maintenance window to enable flag and monitor metrics (connection churn, reconnection rate). If reconnects go down, we'll keep it, else revert.
amar (billing): I'll draft customer-facing note explaining reconnect-driven billing increases and we'll propose a waiver if this was unexpected.
maria (support): Customer ok with a staged test, asked us to proceed. Provided contact for live debug session tomorrow.
sre-bot: alert: stream-churn high for tenant acropay detected (5xx-rate=0.4%, reconnections=23/min)
ryan (oncall): Noted. Maya, ETA on flag roll?
maya (eng-runtime): I'll have the flag toggled in staging in ~45m and monitor logs for short-writes. If looks good, push to prod in the maintenance window.
maria (support): thanks team — I'll schedule the debug call and keep AcroPay updated. will close thread when we confirm reduced reconnections. :thumbsup:
